     2	
     3	The implementation intentionally keeps RecBole3.0's contracts: Euclidean
     4	residual quantization, optional Sinkhorn assignment on the last level, and

    20	class MLP(nn.Module):
    21	    """RecBole3.0's dropout/linear/ReLU MLP helper."""
    22	
    23	    def __init__(self, hidden_sizes: list[int], dropout: float = 0.0):
    24	        super().__init__()
    25	        modules: list[nn.Module] = []

    27	            modules.extend((nn.Dropout(p=dropout), nn.Linear(input_size, output_size), nn.ReLU()))

    44	class VQLayer(nn.Module):
    45	    """Trainable vector quantizer from RecBole3.0."""
    46	
    47	    def __init__(
    48	        self,
    49	        codebook_size: int,
    50	        codebook_dim: int,
    51	        beta: float = 0.25,
    52	        sk_epsilon: float = -1.0,
    53	        sk_iters: int = -1,
    54	    ):
    55	        super().__init__()
    56	        self.dim = int(codebook_dim)
    57	        self.n_embed = int(codebook_size)
    58	        self.beta = float(beta)
    59	        self.use_sk = sk_epsilon > 0 and sk_iters > 0
    60	        self.sk_epsilon = float(sk_epsilon)
    61	        self.sk_iters = int(sk_iters)
    62	        self.embed = nn.Embedding(self.n_embed, self.dim)
    63	
    64	    def get_code_embs(self) -> nn.Parameter:

    66	
    67	    def _copy_init_embed(self, init_embed: torch.Tensor) -> None:

    69	
    70	    @staticmethod
    71	    def center_distance(distances: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    72	        max_distance = distances.max()
    73	        min_distance = distances.min()
    74	        middle = (max_distance + min_distance) / 2
    75	        amplitude = max_distance - middle + 1e-5
    76	        if not bool(amplitude > 0):
    77	            raise ValueError("Cannot center a constant distance matrix.")
    78	        return (distances - middle) / amplitude
    79	
    80	    @staticmethod
    81	    def _balanced_assignment(logits: torch.Tensor, epsilon: float, iterations: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    82	        """Differentiable Sinkhorn balancing of the coupled assignment logits."""
    83	        q = torch.softmax(-logits / max(epsilon, 1e-6), dim=-1)
    84	        for _ in range(int(iterations)):
    85	            q = q / q.sum(dim=0, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
    86	            q = q / q.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
    87	        return q
    88	
    89	    @torch.no_grad()
    90	    def sinkhorn(
    91	        self,
    92	        distances: torch.Tensor,
    93	        epsilon: float = 0.003,
    94	        iterations: int = 5,
    95	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
    96	        q = torch.exp(-distances / epsilon)
    97	        batch_size, codebook_size = q.shape
    98	        q /= q.sum(-1, keepdim=True).sum(-2, keepdim=True)
    99	        for _ in range(iterations):
   100	            q /= q.sum(0, keepdim=True)
   101	            q /= codebook_size
   102	            q /= q.sum(1, keepdim=True)
   103	            q /= batch_size
   104	        q *= batch_size
   105	        return q
   106	
   107	    def _distances(self, latent: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   108	        code_embs = self.get_code_embs()
   109	        return (
   110	            latent.pow(2).sum(1, keepdim=True)
   111	            - 2 * latent @ code_embs.t()
   112	            + code_embs.pow(2).sum(1, keepdim=True).t()
   113	        )
   114	
   115	    def _indices(self, distances: torch.Tensor, infer_use_sk: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
   116	        if (self.training and self.use_sk) or (self.use_sk and infer_use_sk):
   117	            centered = self.center_distance(distances).double()
   118	            q = self.sinkhorn(centered, self.sk_epsilon, self.sk_iters)
   119	            if torch.isnan(q).any() or torch.isinf(q).any():
   120	                raise RuntimeError("Sinkhorn assignment returned NaN or infinity.")
   121	            return torch.argmax(q, dim=-1)
   122	        return torch.argmin(distances, dim=-1)
   123	
   124	    def forward(
   125	        self,
   126	        x: torch.Tensor,
   127	        infer_use_sk: bool = False,
   128	        assignment_logits: torch.Tensor | None = None,
   129	    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, int, torch.Tensor]:
   130	        latent = x.view(-1, self.dim)
   131	        distances = self._distances(latent)
   132	        if assignment_logits is not None:
   133	            if assignment_logits.shape != distances.shape:
   134	                raise ValueError(
   135	                    f"assignment_logits must have shape {tuple(distances.shape)}, "
   136	                    f"got {tuple(assignment_logits.shape)}"
   137	                )
   138	            if not torch.isfinite(assignment_logits).all():
   139	                raise ValueError("assignment_logits must be finite")
   140	        # Balance the coupled assignment. Sinkhorn normalisation gives the batch
   141	        # a near-uniform code marginal, which makes a collapsed solution (one
   142	        # bucket absorbing the catalogue) infeasible; that is what lets the
   143	        # behaviour/curvature term enter at full strength without the runaway
   144	        # collapse the first iteration measured (largest L1 bucket 98.5%).
   145	        if assignment_logits is not None and getattr(self, "balanced_assignment", False):
   146	            # Differentiable balancing. The class's own sinkhorn() is decorated
   147	            # @torch.no_grad() because it only ever produced a hard index; using
   148	            # it here would cut the soft assignment objective off the graph and
   149	            # turn the coupled term into a dead one. This variant keeps the
   150	            # gradient and produces rows that sum to one, so log(q).softmax()
   151	            # below recovers q exactly.
   152	            balanced = self._balanced_assignment(
   153	                assignment_logits.double(), self.sk_epsilon, self.sk_iters)
   154	            if torch.isnan(balanced).any() or torch.isinf(balanced).any():
   155	                raise RuntimeError("Balanced assignment returned NaN or infinity.")
   156	            assignment_logits = torch.log(balanced.clamp_min(1e-12)).to(assignment_logits.dtype)
   157	        embed_ind = (assignment_logits.argmax(-1) if assignment_logits is not None
   158	                     else self._indices(distances, infer_use_sk))
   159	        onehot = F.one_hot(embed_ind, self.n_embed)
   160	        used = onehot.sum(0)
   161	        # Skip the DDP all_reduce when running inference on rank 0 only:
   162	        # the unused-code accounting is a per-rank stat, and a single-rank
   163	        # all_reduce would deadlock waiting for the other 3 ranks to join.
   164	        if distributed.is_initialized() and infer_use_sk is False and not getattr(self, "_skip_ddp_reduce", False):

   166	        unused_codes = int((used == 0).sum().item())
   167	
   168	        hard_q = F.embedding(embed_ind, self.get_code_embs())
   169	        soft = assignment_logits.softmax(-1) @ self.get_code_embs() if assignment_logits is not None else None
   170	        x_q = hard_q.view(x.shape)
   171	        quant_loss = F.mse_loss(x_q, x.detach()) + self.beta * F.mse_loss(x, x_q.detach())

   173	            # Train the actual soft candidate distribution as well as using it
   174	            # for the straight-through decoder path. This keeps assignment
   175	            # logits in the optimized objective even if reconstruction grads
   176	            # through the decoder are small.
   177	            quant_loss = quant_loss + F.mse_loss(soft.view(x.shape), x.detach())
   178	        x_q = x + (x_q - x).detach()
   179	        if soft is not None:
   180	            soft = soft.view(x.shape)
   181	            x_q = x_q + soft - soft.detach()
   182	        return x_q, quant_loss, unused_codes, embed_ind.view(*x.shape[:-1])
   183	
   184	    def embed_code(self, embed_id: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   185	        return F.embedding(embed_id, self.get_code_embs())
   186	
   187	    def init_codebook(self, x: torch.Tensor, device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
   188	        kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=self.n_embed, n_init="auto").fit(x.detach().cpu().numpy())
   189	        centers = torch.tensor(kmeans.cluster_centers_, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
   190	        if distributed.is_initialized():
   191	            distributed.broadcast(centers, 0)
   192	        self._copy_init_embed(centers.clone())
   193	        embed_ind = torch.argmin(self._distances(x), dim=-1).view(*x.shape[:-1])
   194	        return x - self.embed_code(embed_ind)

   197	class EMAVQLayer(VQLayer):
   198	    """EMA variant from RecBole3.0."""
   199	
   200	    def __init__(
   201	        self,
   202	        codebook_size: int,

   219	    def _copy_init_embed(self, init_embed: torch.Tensor) -> None:
   220	        self.embed.data.copy_(init_embed)
   221	        self.embed_avg.data.copy_(init_embed)
   222	        self.cluster_size.data.copy_(torch.ones(self.n_embed, device=init_embed.device))
   223	
   224	    def get_code_embs(self) -> nn.Parameter:
   225	        return self.embed
   226	
   227	    def forward(
   228	        self,
   229	        x: torch.Tensor,
   230	        infer_use_sk: bool = False,
   231	        first_assignment_logits: torch.Tensor | None = None,
   232	    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, int, torch.Tensor]:
   233	        latent = x.view(-1, self.dim)
   234	        embed_ind = self._indices(self._distances(latent), infer_use_sk)

   236	
   237	        if self.training:
   238	            onehot = F.one_hot(embed_ind, self.n_embed).type(latent.dtype)
   239	            used = onehot.sum(0)
   240	            embed_sum = onehot.t() @ latent
   241	            if distributed.is_initialized():
   242	                distributed.all_reduce(used, op=distributed.ReduceOp.SUM)

   246	            self.embed_avg.data.mul_(self.decay).add_(embed_sum, alpha=1 - self.decay)
   247	            n = self.cluster_size.sum()
   248	            norm_w = n * (self.cluster_size + self.eps) / (n + self.n_embed * self.eps)
   249	            self.embed.data.copy_(self.embed_avg / norm_w.unsqueeze(1))
   250	        else:

   121	def _stable_squared_poincare_from_arg(arg: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   122	    """Evaluate acosh(1 + arg)^2 with its differentiable zero limit."""
   123	    stable_arg = arg.clamp(min=0.0, max=1e6)
   124	    # sqrt itself has an infinite derivative at zero. A tiny floor inside the
   125	    # root prevents 0 * inf in autograd; its squared-distance bias is < 2e-12.
   126	    root_arg = (stable_arg * 0.5).clamp_min(1e-12)
   127	    value = 4.0 * torch.asinh(torch.sqrt(root_arg)).square()
   128	    # Keep the graph connected at exact coincidence: a torch.where against a
   129	    # constant zero selects a branch with no gradient, so a codepoint that sits
   130	    # exactly on a barycentre would silently stop training that pair. Subtract
   131	    # the value the floor adds instead, which is exactly zero at arg == 0 and
   132	    # carries the derivative of the asinh form everywhere.
   133	    floor_value = 4.0 * float(torch.asinh(torch.sqrt(torch.tensor(1e-12))).square())
   134	    return (value - floor_value).clamp_min(0.0)

   137	def incoming_assignment_loss(model: RQVAE, batch_ids: torch.Tensor,
   138	                             bary: torch.Tensor, neg_bary: torch.Tensor,
   139	                             embeddings: torch.Tensor,
   140	                             behaviour_on: bool = True, geometry: str = "poincare",
   141	                             concentration: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> torch.Tensor:
   142	    """Contrast code candidates against the cached train-only predecessor barycentres.
   143	
   144	    The barycentres are refreshed once per epoch from the current codebook (see
   145	    ``refresh_context_barycentres``), so this function is one broadcast distance
   146	    per candidate and stays vectorised over the batch. The behaviour signal and
   147	    the curved contrast themselves are unchanged: only the per-item Python loop
   148	    that recomputed a Frechet mean for every sample of every step was removed.
   149	    """
   150	    layer = model.rq.vq_layers[0]
   151	    codes = layer.get_code_embs()
   152	    x = model.encoder(embeddings[batch_ids])
   153	    eps = 1e-5
   154	    if not behaviour_on:
   155	        # behaviour-off control: the plain reconstruction-consistent Euclidean
   156	        # cost of the item's own latent. Nothing is detached, so the control
   157	        # keeps the same gradient path as the coupled arm and differs only in
   158	        # the behaviour/curvature term -- a detached control would compare two
   159	        # different graphs instead of one graph with and without the term.
   160	        control_cost = (x.square().sum(-1)[:, None] + codes.square().sum(-1)[None, :]
   161	                        - 2.0 * (x @ codes.t())).clamp_min(0.0)
   162	        return -control_cost / CONTEXT_TEMPERATURE
   163	
   164	    def project(z):
   165	        norm = z.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-8)
   166	        return z / norm * torch.tanh(norm * 0.5) * (1.0 - eps)
   167	
   168	    def distance(a, b):
   169	        # |a-b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2 - 2 a.b: the broadcast form materialised a
   170	        # (batch, codebook, dim) tensor and cost 7 s per epoch, the identity is
   171	        # the same number and costs one matmul.
   172	        if geometry == "euclidean":
   173	            return (a.square().sum(-1)[:, None] + b.square().sum(-1)[None, :]
   174	                    - 2.0 * (a @ b.t())).clamp_min(0.0)
   175	        a, b = project(a), project(b)
   176	        delta_sq = (a.square().sum(-1)[:, None] + b.square().sum(-1)[None, :]
   177	                    - 2.0 * (a @ b.t())).clamp_min(0.0)
   178	        an = a.norm(dim=-1).clamp(max=1 - eps)
   179	        bn = b.norm(dim=-1).clamp(max=1 - eps)
   180	        arg = (2 * delta_sq / ((1 - an.square())[:, None] * (1 - bn.square())[None, :])).clamp_min(0)
   181	        # acosh(1 + arg) has an infinite derivative at arg=0.  The identity
   182	        # acosh(1 + z) = 2 asinh(sqrt(z / 2)) has a finite derivative after
   183	        # squaring: d^2/dz -> 2 as z -> 0.  Clamp only the upper range; preserve
   184	        # the exact zero limit so coincident points have exactly zero distance.
   185	        return _stable_squared_poincare_from_arg(arg)
   186	
   187	    positive = bary[batch_ids]
   188	    negative = neg_bary[batch_ids]
   189	    # MODULATE, do not replace. The first iteration let the behaviour/curvature
   190	    # cost replace the assignment entirely, so the argmax drifted to the few
   191	    # codes nearest the barycentre and the first level collapsed into one bucket
   192	    # holding 98.5% of the catalogue (cooccur_overlap_L3 0.0584 against the
   193	    # 0.0756 baseline). The reconstruction-consistent squared Euclidean cost is
   194	    # therefore the base term again and the geodesic contrast enters as a
   195	    # zero-centred, unit-scale bias, weighted by the concentration gate and by
   196	    # CONTEXT_WEIGHT: the Euclidean term still orders the codes, the behaviour
   197	    # term only re-weights them, and no single bucket can absorb the catalogue.
   198	    euclidean_cost = (x.square().sum(-1)[:, None] + codes.square().sum(-1)[None, :]
   199	                      - 2.0 * (x @ codes.t())).clamp_min(0.0)
   200	    behaviour_cost = distance(positive, codes) - 0.5 * distance(negative, codes)
   201	    bias = behaviour_cost - behaviour_cost.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
   202	    bias = bias / bias.abs().mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(eps)
   203	    gate = (concentration[batch_ids].unsqueeze(-1) if concentration is not None
   204	            else torch.ones_like(bias[:, :1]))
   205	    # Iteration 3: with the Sinkhorn balance active on the assignment the
   206	    # behaviour/curvature cost can enter at full strength; the balance, not a
   207	    # small weight, is what prevents the collapse.
   208	    if BALANCED_ASSIGNMENT:
   209	        scores = gate * behaviour_cost + (1.0 - gate) * euclidean_cost
   210	    else:
   211	        scores = euclidean_cost + CONTEXT_WEIGHT * gate * bias
   212	    return -scores / CONTEXT_TEMPERATURE

   215	def build_context_tables(incoming_sparse, hard_negative, item_count: int, device):
   216	    """Pad the train-only predecessor lists and hard negatives into dense tensors."""
   217	    slots = 8
   218	    index = torch.zeros((item_count, slots), dtype=torch.long)
   219	    weight = torch.zeros((item_count, slots), dtype=torch.float32)
   220	    mask = torch.zeros((item_count, slots), dtype=torch.bool)
   221	    for item, values in incoming_sparse.items():
   222	        if not 0 <= int(item) < item_count:
   223	            continue
   224	        values = values[:slots]
   225	        total = float(sum(v for _, v in values)) or 1.0
   226	        for slot, (predecessor, count) in enumerate(values):
   227	            index[int(item), slot] = int(predecessor)
   228	            weight[int(item), slot] = float(count) / total
   229	            mask[int(item), slot] = True
   230	    negative = torch.arange(item_count, dtype=torch.long)
   231	    for item, value in hard_negative.items():
   232	        if 0 <= int(item) < item_count:
   233	            negative[int(item)] = int(value)
   234	    return index.to(device), weight.to(device), mask.to(device), negative.to(device)

   237	def refresh_context_barycentres(model, embeddings, index, weight, mask, negative, device,
   238	                                geometry: str = "poincare"):
   239	    """Per-epoch Frechet mean of the predecessors' codepoints, for every item.
   240	
   241	    The predecessor identities are frozen (train-only); only the codepoints move,
   242	    so the barycentres are recomputed once per epoch instead of once per sample
   243	    per step. ``log0``/``project`` keep the mean inside the ball.
   244	    """
   245	    # unwrap DDP before reaching for the codebook: called with the wrapper this
   246	    # raised "'DistributedDataParallel' object has no attribute 'rq'" on every
   247	    # rank, and the one-rank smoke never exercised it
   248	    raw = model.module if hasattr(model, "module") else model
   249	    layer = raw.rq.vq_layers[0]
   250	    eps = 1e-5
   251	
   252	    def project(z):
   253	        norm = z.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-8)
   254	        return z / norm * torch.tanh(norm * 0.5) * (1.0 - eps)
   255	
   256	    def log_map(base, point):
   257	        diff = mobius_add(-base, point)
   258	        norm = diff.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(eps)
   259	        bn = base.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp(max=1.0 - eps)
   260	        scale = 2.0 / (1.0 - bn.square()).clamp_min(eps)
   261	        return scale * torch.atanh(norm.clamp(max=1.0 - eps)) * diff / norm
   262	
   263	    def mobius_add(a, b):
   264	        aa = a.square().sum(-1, keepdim=True); bb = b.square().sum(-1, keepdim=True)
   265	        ab = (a * b).sum(-1, keepdim=True)
   266	        numerator = (1 + 2 * ab + bb) * a + (1 - aa) * b
   267	        denominator = (1 + 2 * ab + aa * bb).clamp_min(eps)
   268	        return project(numerator / denominator)
   269	
   270	    def exp_map(base, tangent):
   271	        bn = base.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
   272	        tn = tangent.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(eps)
   273	        scaled = torch.tanh((1.0 - bn.square()).clamp_min(eps) * tn / 2) * tangent / tn
   274	        return mobius_add(base, scaled)
   275	
   276	    with torch.no_grad():
   277	        codes = layer.get_code_embs().detach()
   278	        curved_codes = project(codes)
   279	        flat = index.reshape(-1)
   280	        unique, inverse = torch.unique(flat, return_inverse=True)
   281	        encoded = raw.encoder(embeddings[unique])
   282	        if geometry == "euclidean":
   283	            region = torch.cdist(encoded, codes).argmin(-1)
   284	        else:
   285	            points = project(encoded)
   286	            c = project(codes)
   287	            delta = torch.cdist(points, c).square().clamp_min(0)
   288	            pn = points.norm(dim=-1).clamp(max=1-eps); cn = c.norm(dim=-1).clamp(max=1-eps)
   289	            d = torch.acosh(1 + (2 * delta / ((1-pn.square())[:, None] * (1-cn.square())[None, :]).clamp_min(eps)).clamp(0, 1e6))
   290	            region = d.argmin(-1)
   291	        regions = region[inverse].view_as(index)
   292	        weights = (weight * mask.float()).unsqueeze(-1)
   293	        def frechet_mean(reg):
   294	            # geometry-off must remove the curvature from the barycentre too, not
   295	            # only from the region choice: the Euclidean control averages the raw
   296	            # codepoints and skips the Karcher iterations entirely.
   297	            if geometry == "euclidean":
   298	                pts = codes[reg]
   299	                w = weights.expand_as(pts)
   300	                return (w * pts).sum(1) / w.sum(1).clamp_min(eps)
   301	            pts = curved_codes[reg]
   302	            w = weights.expand_as(pts)
   303	            mean = project((w * pts).sum(1) / w.sum(1).clamp_min(eps))
   304	            for _ in range(8):
   305	                tangent = log_map(mean[:, None, :].expand_as(pts), pts)
   306	                step = (w * tangent).sum(1) / w.sum(1).clamp_min(eps)
   307	                mean = exp_map(mean, 0.5 * step)
   308	            return mean
   309	        bary = frechet_mean(regions)
   310	        negative_regions = regions[negative]
   311	        neg_bary = frechet_mean(negative_regions)
   312	        # Concentration is over predecessor *regions*, not predecessor IDs:
   313	        # aggregate each item's normalized incoming mass by its detached region.
   314	        # Include all first-codebook regions in the entropy normalization, even
   315	        # when a particular item has zero mass in some regions.
   316	        region_count = curved_codes.shape[0]
   317	        probs = (weight * mask.float()).clamp_min(0)
   318	        probs = probs / probs.sum(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(eps)
   319	        region_mass = probs.new_zeros((probs.shape[0], region_count))
   320	        region_mass.scatter_add_(1, regions.long(), probs)
   321	        entropy_terms = torch.where(
   322	            region_mass > 0,
   323	            region_mass * region_mass.clamp_min(eps).log(),
   324	            torch.zeros_like(region_mass),
   325	        )
   326	        entropy = -entropy_terms.sum(-1)
   327	        concentration = (1.0 - entropy / math.log(max(region_count, 2))).clamp(0, 1)
   328	        # An item with no observed training predecessor has an all-zero mask: its
   329	        # region mass is empty, its entropy is zero, and the formula above would
   330	        # call that "maximally concentrated" while its barycentre is the zero
   331	        # vector. Such an item must fall back to the plain Euclidean assignment,
   332	        # so the gate is forced to zero wherever no context exists.
   333	        has_context = mask.any(dim=-1).to(concentration.dtype)
   334	        concentration = concentration * has_context
   335	    return bary.detach(), neg_bary.detach(), concentration.detach()

   380	def load_embeddings(path: Path) -> np.ndarray:
   381	    """Load an (N, D) item-embedding matrix.
   382	
   383	    Accepts either:
   384	    - a Parquet frame with an ``embedding`` column of per-row arrays

   423	def _extend_collisions(tokens: np.ndarray, codebook_sizes: list[int]) -> np.ndarray:
   424	    """Match RecBole3.0's extend path with one fixed extra SID level."""
   425	    if tokens.ndim != 2 or tokens.shape[1] != len(codebook_sizes):
   426	        raise ValueError(f"Token shape {tokens.shape} disagrees with codebook sizes {codebook_sizes}")
   427	    groups: dict[tuple[int, ...], list[int]] = {}
   428	    for item_id, row in enumerate(tokens.tolist()):
   429	        groups.setdefault(tuple(int(value) for value in row), []).append(item_id)
   430	    offsets = np.cumsum([0, *codebook_sizes], dtype=np.int64)
   431	    result = np.empty((len(tokens), tokens.shape[1] + 1), dtype=np.int64)
   432	    for row, item_ids in groups.items():
   433	        for occurrence, item_id in enumerate(item_ids):
   434	            result[item_id, :-1] = np.asarray(row, dtype=np.int64)
   435	            result[item_id, -1] = int(offsets[-1] + occurrence)
   436	    return result

   129	    # constant zero selects a branch with no gradient, so a codepoint that sits
   130	    # exactly on a barycentre would silently stop training that pair. Subtract
   131	    # the value the floor adds instead, which is exactly zero at arg == 0 and
   132	    # carries the derivative of the asinh form everywhere.

   137	def incoming_assignment_loss(model: RQVAE, batch_ids: torch.Tensor,
   138	                             bary: torch.Tensor, neg_bary: torch.Tensor,
   139	                             embeddings: torch.Tensor,
   140	                             behaviour_on: bool = True, geometry: str = "poincare",
   141	                             concentration: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> torch.Tensor:
   142	    """Contrast code candidates against the cached train-only predecessor barycentres.
   143	
   144	    The barycentres are refreshed once per epoch from the current codebook (see
   145	    ``refresh_context_barycentres``), so this function is one broadcast distance
   146	    per candidate and stays vectorised over the batch. The behaviour signal and
   147	    the curved contrast themselves are unchanged: only the per-item Python loop
   148	    that recomputed a Frechet mean for every sample of every step was removed.
   149	    """
   150	    layer = model.rq.vq_layers[0]
   151	    codes = layer.get_code_embs()
   152	    x = model.encoder(embeddings[batch_ids])
   153	    eps = 1e-5
   154	    if not behaviour_on:
   155	        # behaviour-off control: the plain reconstruction-consistent Euclidean
   156	        # cost of the item's own latent. Nothing is detached, so the control
   157	        # keeps the same gradient path as the coupled arm and differs only in
   158	        # the behaviour/curvature term -- a detached control would compare two
   159	        # different graphs instead of one graph with and without the term.
   160	        control_cost = (x.square().sum(-1)[:, None] + codes.square().sum(-1)[None, :]
   161	                        - 2.0 * (x @ codes.t())).clamp_min(0.0)
   162	        return -control_cost / CONTEXT_TEMPERATURE
   163	
   164	    def project(z):
   165	        norm = z.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-8)
   166	        return z / norm * torch.tanh(norm * 0.5) * (1.0 - eps)
   167	
   168	    def distance(a, b):
   169	        # |a-b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2 - 2 a.b: the broadcast form materialised a
   170	        # (batch, codebook, dim) tensor and cost 7 s per epoch, the identity is
   171	        # the same number and costs one matmul.
   172	        if geometry == "euclidean":
   173	            return (a.square().sum(-1)[:, None] + b.square().sum(-1)[None, :]
   174	                    - 2.0 * (a @ b.t())).clamp_min(0.0)
   175	        a, b = project(a), project(b)
   176	        delta_sq = (a.square().sum(-1)[:, None] + b.square().sum(-1)[None, :]
   177	                    - 2.0 * (a @ b.t())).clamp_min(0.0)
   178	        an = a.norm(dim=-1).clamp(max=1 - eps)
   179	        bn = b.norm(dim=-1).clamp(max=1 - eps)
   180	        arg = (2 * delta_sq / ((1 - an.square())[:, None] * (1 - bn.square())[None, :])).clamp_min(0)
   181	        # acosh(1 + arg) has an infinite derivative at arg=0.  The identity
   182	        # acosh(1 + z) = 2 asinh(sqrt(z / 2)) has a finite derivative after
   183	        # squaring: d^2/dz -> 2 as z -> 0.  Clamp only the upper range; preserve
   184	        # the exact zero limit so coincident points have exactly zero distance.
   185	        return _stable_squared_poincare_from_arg(arg)
   186	
   187	    positive = bary[batch_ids]
   188	    negative = neg_bary[batch_ids]
   189	    # MODULATE, do not replace. The first iteration let the behaviour/curvature
   190	    # cost replace the assignment entirely, so the argmax drifted to the few
   191	    # codes nearest the barycentre and the first level collapsed into one bucket
   192	    # holding 98.5% of the catalogue (cooccur_overlap_L3 0.0584 against the
   193	    # 0.0756 baseline). The reconstruction-consistent squared Euclidean cost is
   194	    # therefore the base term again and the geodesic contrast enters as a
   195	    # zero-centred, unit-scale bias, weighted by the concentration gate and by
   196	    # CONTEXT_WEIGHT: the Euclidean term still orders the codes, the behaviour
   197	    # term only re-weights them, and no single bucket can absorb the catalogue.
   198	    euclidean_cost = (x.square().sum(-1)[:, None] + codes.square().sum(-1)[None, :]
   199	                      - 2.0 * (x @ codes.t())).clamp_min(0.0)
   200	    behaviour_cost = distance(positive, codes) - 0.5 * distance(negative, codes)
   201	    bias = behaviour_cost - behaviour_cost.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
   202	    bias = bias / bias.abs().mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(eps)
   203	    gate = (concentration[batch_ids].unsqueeze(-1) if concentration is not None
   204	            else torch.ones_like(bias[:, :1]))
   205	    # Iteration 3: with the Sinkhorn balance active on the assignment the
   206	    # behaviour/curvature cost can enter at full strength; the balance, not a
   207	    # small weight, is what prevents the collapse.
   208	    if BALANCED_ASSIGNMENT:
   209	        scores = gate * behaviour_cost + (1.0 - gate) * euclidean_cost
   210	    else:
   211	        scores = euclidean_cost + CONTEXT_WEIGHT * gate * bias
   212	    return -scores / CONTEXT_TEMPERATURE

   215	def build_context_tables(incoming_sparse, hard_negative, item_count: int, device):
   216	    """Pad the train-only predecessor lists and hard negatives into dense tensors."""
   217	    slots = 8
   218	    index = torch.zeros((item_count, slots), dtype=torch.long)
   219	    weight = torch.zeros((item_count, slots), dtype=torch.float32)
   220	    mask = torch.zeros((item_count, slots), dtype=torch.bool)
   221	    for item, values in incoming_sparse.items():
   222	        if not 0 <= int(item) < item_count:
   223	            continue
   224	        values = values[:slots]
   225	        total = float(sum(v for _, v in values)) or 1.0
   226	        for slot, (predecessor, count) in enumerate(values):
   227	            index[int(item), slot] = int(predecessor)
   228	            weight[int(item), slot] = float(count) / total
   229	            mask[int(item), slot] = True
   230	    negative = torch.arange(item_count, dtype=torch.long)
   231	    for item, value in hard_negative.items():
   232	        if 0 <= int(item) < item_count:
   233	            negative[int(item)] = int(value)
   234	    return index.to(device), weight.to(device), mask.to(device), negative.to(device)

   237	def refresh_context_barycentres(model, embeddings, index, weight, mask, negative, device,
   238	                                geometry: str = "poincare"):
   239	    """Per-epoch Frechet mean of the predecessors' codepoints, for every item.
   240	
   241	    The predecessor identities are frozen (train-only); only the codepoints move,
   242	    so the barycentres are recomputed once per epoch instead of once per sample
   243	    per step. ``log0``/``project`` keep the mean inside the ball.
   244	    """
   245	    # unwrap DDP before reaching for the codebook: called with the wrapper this
   246	    # raised "'DistributedDataParallel' object has no attribute 'rq'" on every
   247	    # rank, and the one-rank smoke never exercised it
   248	    raw = model.module if hasattr(model, "module") else model
   249	    layer = raw.rq.vq_layers[0]
   250	    eps = 1e-5
   251	
   252	    def project(z):
   253	        norm = z.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-8)
   254	        return z / norm * torch.tanh(norm * 0.5) * (1.0 - eps)
   255	
   256	    def log_map(base, point):
   257	        diff = mobius_add(-base, point)
   258	        norm = diff.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(eps)
   259	        bn = base.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp(max=1.0 - eps)
   260	        scale = 2.0 / (1.0 - bn.square()).clamp_min(eps)
   261	        return scale * torch.atanh(norm.clamp(max=1.0 - eps)) * diff / norm
   262	
   263	    def mobius_add(a, b):
   264	        aa = a.square().sum(-1, keepdim=True); bb = b.square().sum(-1, keepdim=True)
   265	        ab = (a * b).sum(-1, keepdim=True)
   266	        numerator = (1 + 2 * ab + bb) * a + (1 - aa) * b
   267	        denominator = (1 + 2 * ab + aa * bb).clamp_min(eps)
   268	        return project(numerator / denominator)
   269	
   270	    def exp_map(base, tangent):
   271	        bn = base.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
   272	        tn = tangent.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(eps)
   273	        scaled = torch.tanh((1.0 - bn.square()).clamp_min(eps) * tn / 2) * tangent / tn
   274	        return mobius_add(base, scaled)
   275	
   276	    with torch.no_grad():
   277	        codes = layer.get_code_embs().detach()
   278	        curved_codes = project(codes)
   279	        flat = index.reshape(-1)
   280	        unique, inverse = torch.unique(flat, return_inverse=True)
   281	        encoded = raw.encoder(embeddings[unique])
   282	        if geometry == "euclidean":
   283	            region = torch.cdist(encoded, codes).argmin(-1)
   284	        else:
   285	            points = project(encoded)
   286	            c = project(codes)
   287	            delta = torch.cdist(points, c).square().clamp_min(0)
   288	            pn = points.norm(dim=-1).clamp(max=1-eps); cn = c.norm(dim=-1).clamp(max=1-eps)
   289	            d = torch.acosh(1 + (2 * delta / ((1-pn.square())[:, None] * (1-cn.square())[None, :]).clamp_min(eps)).clamp(0, 1e6))
   290	            region = d.argmin(-1)
   291	        regions = region[inverse].view_as(index)
   292	        weights = (weight * mask.float()).unsqueeze(-1)
   293	        def frechet_mean(reg):
   294	            # geometry-off must remove the curvature from the barycentre too, not
   295	            # only from the region choice: the Euclidean control averages the raw
   296	            # codepoints and skips the Karcher iterations entirely.
   297	            if geometry == "euclidean":
   298	                pts = codes[reg]
   299	                w = weights.expand_as(pts)
   300	                return (w * pts).sum(1) / w.sum(1).clamp_min(eps)
   301	            pts = curved_codes[reg]
   302	            w = weights.expand_as(pts)
   303	            mean = project((w * pts).sum(1) / w.sum(1).clamp_min(eps))
   304	            for _ in range(8):
   305	                tangent = log_map(mean[:, None, :].expand_as(pts), pts)
   306	                step = (w * tangent).sum(1) / w.sum(1).clamp_min(eps)
   307	                mean = exp_map(mean, 0.5 * step)
   308	            return mean
   309	        bary = frechet_mean(regions)
   310	        negative_regions = regions[negative]
   311	        neg_bary = frechet_mean(negative_regions)
   312	        # Concentration is over predecessor *regions*, not predecessor IDs:
   313	        # aggregate each item's normalized incoming mass by its detached region.
   314	        # Include all first-codebook regions in the entropy normalization, even
   315	        # when a particular item has zero mass in some regions.
   316	        region_count = curved_codes.shape[0]
   317	        probs = (weight * mask.float()).clamp_min(0)
   318	        probs = probs / probs.sum(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(eps)
   319	        region_mass = probs.new_zeros((probs.shape[0], region_count))
   320	        region_mass.scatter_add_(1, regions.long(), probs)
   321	        entropy_terms = torch.where(
   322	            region_mass > 0,
   323	            region_mass * region_mass.clamp_min(eps).log(),
   324	            torch.zeros_like(region_mass),
   325	        )
   326	        entropy = -entropy_terms.sum(-1)
   327	        concentration = (1.0 - entropy / math.log(max(region_count, 2))).clamp(0, 1)
   328	        # An item with no observed training predecessor has an all-zero mask: its
   329	        # region mass is empty, its entropy is zero, and the formula above would
   330	        # call that "maximally concentrated" while its barycentre is the zero
   331	        # vector. Such an item must fall back to the plain Euclidean assignment,
   332	        # so the gate is forced to zero wherever no context exists.
   333	        has_context = mask.any(dim=-1).to(concentration.dtype)
   334	        concentration = concentration * has_context
   335	    return bary.detach(), neg_bary.detach(), concentration.detach()

   423	def _extend_collisions(tokens: np.ndarray, codebook_sizes: list[int]) -> np.ndarray:
   424	    """Match RecBole3.0's extend path with one fixed extra SID level."""
   425	    if tokens.ndim != 2 or tokens.shape[1] != len(codebook_sizes):
   426	        raise ValueError(f"Token shape {tokens.shape} disagrees with codebook sizes {codebook_sizes}")
   427	    groups: dict[tuple[int, ...], list[int]] = {}
   428	    for item_id, row in enumerate(tokens.tolist()):
   429	        groups.setdefault(tuple(int(value) for value in row), []).append(item_id)
   430	    offsets = np.cumsum([0, *codebook_sizes], dtype=np.int64)
   431	    result = np.empty((len(tokens), tokens.shape[1] + 1), dtype=np.int64)
   432	    for row, item_ids in groups.items():
   433	        for occurrence, item_id in enumerate(item_ids):
   434	            result[item_id, :-1] = np.asarray(row, dtype=np.int64)
   435	            result[item_id, -1] = int(offsets[-1] + occurrence)
   436	    return result

   476	    train_ids = np.unique(train_frame["target"].to_numpy(dtype=np.int64))

   478	        raise ValueError("Training target item ids do not match the embedding rows")

   480	    all_embeddings = torch.from_numpy(embeddings)
   481	    train_embeddings = all_embeddings[torch.from_numpy(train_ids)]
   482	    # Adjacent history->target events define directed training-only counts.
   483	    incoming: dict[int, dict[int, int]] = {}
   484	    user_items: dict[int, set[int]] = {}
   485	    transitioned: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
   486	    for row in train_frame.itertuples(index=False):
   487	        target = int(row.target); history = [int(v) for v in row.history]
   488	        user_items.setdefault(int(row.user), set()).add(target)
   489	        if history:
   490	            pred = history[-1]
   491	            incoming.setdefault(target, {})[pred] = incoming.setdefault(target, {}).get(pred, 0) + 1
   492	            transitioned.add((pred, target))
   493	    incoming_sparse = {i: sorted(v.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:8] for i,v in incoming.items()}
   494	    # A high-overlap train co-consumption item with no observed incoming edge.
   495	    # The hard negative is the train co-consumption item with the highest Jaccard
   496	    # overlap over users that is *not* an observed predecessor of the item. The
   497	    # overlap is read off the sparse item x item co-consumption matrix instead of
   498	    # intersecting every pair of user sets, which was O(items^2) set work.
   499	    import scipy.sparse as _sp
   500	    rows_: list[int] = []
   501	    cols_: list[int] = []
   502	    data_: list[float] = []
   503	    user_count = np.zeros(len(embeddings), dtype=np.float64)
   504	    for items in user_items.values():
   505	        ordered = sorted(int(v) for v in items if 0 <= int(v) < len(embeddings))
   506	        for value in ordered:
   507	            user_count[value] += 1.0
   508	        for position, left in enumerate(ordered):
   509	            for right in ordered[position + 1:]:
   510	                rows_.append(left); cols_.append(right); data_.append(1.0)
   511	                rows_.append(right); cols_.append(left); data_.append(1.0)
   512	    overlap = _sp.csr_matrix((np.asarray(data_, dtype=np.float32),
   513	                              (np.asarray(rows_), np.asarray(cols_))),

   519	        neighbours = overlap.indices[start:stop]
   520	        counts = overlap.data[start:stop].astype(np.float64)
   521	        if len(neighbours) == 0:
   522	            continue

   524	        jaccard = counts / np.maximum(union, 1.0)

   526	                            for other in neighbours])

   532	            hard_negative[int(item)] = int(neighbours[best])

   537	    if world_size > 1:
